commitResults.messageTitle: Fix search command and parent email issues
commitResults.messageBody:
The search command just fails if a parent's email field is empty, and
users are unable to remove emails with edit-parent, and one student
cannot have more than two parents.

This undermines the functionality of these features, which make the user
experience worse in general.

Let's update the code for email, search and parents to allow for these
features.

This would ensure that such features are kept working properly for a
good user experience.
Fix search command and parent email issues

commitResults.messageTitle: Update manual testing in the DG
commitResults.messageBody:
The DG currently lacks a lot of testing cases that future developers can
do.

This makes Tutoria difficult for new developers to know how to use it
and how it functions.

Let's add testing for undo, redo and searching.

This will ensure that future developers can understand and know how
Tutoria is meant to work.

After alt + tab, pressing keys f or u will open the file or user guide
tabs respectively even though the intended behavior is alt + f/u.

This causes some issues for some users if they use alt + tab to navigate
to other windows.

Let's fix this by changing the fxml and adding code in MainWindow to
explicitly select the tabs necessary.

This will ensure that users wpn't experience such problems.
Fix alt tab issues

commitResults.messageTitle: Fix add-reminder command rejecting inputs issue
commitResults.messageBody:
Add-reminder currently checks for certain inputs and rejects them.
However, allowing those inputs won't cause any harm, and users who want
to use them will be hindered, since the parser already only checks for
"r/" and "at/" and won't care about anything else.

This will cause some users issues if they want to input something like
"switch off a/c".

Let's remove that checker and make the parser only check for "r/" and
"at/" and not bother with anything else.

This will ensure that more value can be added by allowing rather than
restricting certain inputs.

Some error messages pertaining to dates had their full java error
message displayed on Tutoria.

This could freak users out and confuse them on what to do.

Let's change them to simply say that the date they entered in is
invalid.

This will ensure that error messages would guide the user rather than
scare or confuse them.
Fix add reminder rejecting inputs issue
Standardize date error messages

The DG lacks manual testing guides for a majority of the commands in
Tutoria.

This will not effectively guide new developers in working on Tutoria.

Let's add some manual testing areas for managing students and parents to
ensure some guidance is given.

This ensures that users can better understand how Tutoria works so they
can work on it better.

commitResults.messageTitle: Make Esc close the User Guide window
commitResults.messageBody: The help window opened by F1 is a separate window, so the main window's Esc shortcut never reached it and keyboard users had no way to close it. It now hides itself when Esc is pressed. The User Guide and Developer Guide mention the new key, and tests check that Esc closes the window and other keys leave it open.
Make Esc close the User Guide window

commitResults.messageTitle: Shorten minimum session card length to 30 minutes
commitResults.messageBody:
A one-hour minimum made short sessions look much longer than they are.
A 30-minute card is closer to the real length, and its details still
show because they wrap and the day's row grows to fit.

commitResults.messageTitle: Make each session card only as tall as its details
commitResults.messageBody:
Every card on a day used to be stretched to the height of that day's
tallest card, which left short cards mostly empty. Each card is now
only as tall as its details need, and a card that overlaps earlier
cards sits just below them rather than in a fixed-height lane. A
day's row still keeps its standard height unless its cards need more.

A schedule panel test measured the grid off the JavaFX thread, which
could fail at random, so it now measures on the JavaFX thread.
Fix short session cards
